title: Positive Outlook: Union Properties bets big on Dubai’s Motor City
summary: In-house contracting allows for greater control over project execution, quality, scheduling, and cost management, CEO Amer Khansaheb tells Zawya Projects
thbAction: Position THB's pharma CRM and omnichannel HCP engagement workflows to support launch planning, KAM orchestration, and compliant follow-up across India and the Middle East.
contentHtml:
Dubai-listed developer Union Properties has around 6.6 million square feet of unlaunched gross floor area (GFA) in Motor City master development and continues to assess future development opportunities across its land portfolio amid a positive outlook for Dubai’s residential real estate market.

“Our strengthened balance sheet and robust liquidity position provide us with significant financial flexibility to support our development pipeline,” CEO Amer Khansaheb told Zawya Projects.

During the first half of 2026, the developer maintained average cash balances of more than 400 million UAE dirhams ($109 million) after completing its financial transformation and eliminating legacy debt.

Khansaheb said details on the new AED 2 billion ($545 million) residential master-planned community in Motor City, including consultants, launch timelines, and delivery milestones, will be announced later.

Construction is progressing as scheduled at both Takaya and Mirdad in Motor City.

Takaya is on track for handover in the fourth quarter of 2027, while Mirdad is expected to be delivered in the fourth quarter of 2028, he revealed.

Interview excerpts:

How challenging has it been to launch a master-planned community, given that many investors and buyers are adopting a wait-and-watch policy?

While periods of geopolitical uncertainty naturally encourage some buyers to become more selective, what we are seeing today is not a slowdown in demand but a more mature investment environment. Dubai continues to benefit from strong economic fundamentals, sustained population growth, increasing international investor interest and rising demand from end-users.

These factors continue to support healthy market activity, especially with regard to high-quality, master-planned communities that offer long-term lifestyle value as opposed to just residential spaces. Our strategy has always focused on developments that align with long-term market fundamentals rather than short-term market cycles. Going forward, we remain confident in the outlook for well-planned, differentiated developments.

How long have you been working on the new residential project? Do you still have a land bank in Motor City to launch more projects?

The planning and preparation of a master-planned community is a multi-stage process involving concept and schematic design, detailed design, planning, technical studies, and regulatory approvals. The new development represents the next step for our long-term strategy for Motor City – one of Dubai’s most established and successful communities – where we continue to leverage our extensive experience and deep understanding of the market.

In keeping with market demands and our systematic long-term growth strategy, we will also continue to assess future development opportunities across our land portfolio. To date, we have around 6.6 million square feet of GFA in Motor City that is not yet launched.

When do you intend to launch the project for sale? Have you set any timeline for the project’s completion?

The project is currently progressing through the approval process and further details regarding consultants, launch timelines, and delivery milestones will be announced at an appropriate stage. This development is a significant addition to our expanding pipeline and reflects our commitment to creating thoughtfully planned communities that deliver long-term value for residents, investors, and shareholders alike.

How do you plan to fund the new project? Any plans for a sukuk or REIT?

Our strengthened balance sheet and robust liquidity position provide us with significant financial flexibility to support our development pipeline. During the first half of 2026, we maintained average cash balances exceeding AED 400 million, while successfully completing our financial transformation and eliminating legacy debt. These milestones place us in a strong position to invest in future expansion while maintaining a disciplined capital structure.

As for capital market instruments such as a sukuk or REIT, we continually evaluate opportunities that enhance shareholder value. At this stage, however, there are no announcements to share.

Can you share the construction timelines for Takaya and Mirdad developments? When do you plan to hand over these projects?

Construction continues to progress steadily across both developments, in line with our planned schedules. Takaya remains on track for handover during the fourth quarter of 2027, while Mirdad is progressing according to plan with expected delivery in the fourth quarter of 2028.

 Having an in-house contracting capability allows for greater control over project execution, quality, scheduling, and cost management. It facilitates better coordination between development, design, and construction teams, resulting in faster decision-making, improved operational efficiency, and stronger execution discipline during the project lifecycle.

At the same time, our approach remains flexible. We collaborate with external contractors when necessary to ensure each project benefits from the most suitable delivery model.

Ultimately, our priorities remain unchanged – deliver projects on time, maintain the highest quality standards, and create long-term value for our stakeholders.

How important is it now to deliver any project on schedule?

Timely delivery is one of the most important indicators of a developer’s credibility and long-term reputation. Modern buyers and investors place significant value on execution certainty, particularly in a mature real estate market such as Dubai.

We believe timely delivery plays a key role in strengthening customer confidence, reinforcing investor trust, and supporting sustainable business performance. Disciplined execution is central to our strategy and we remain committed to delivering every project with the highest standards of quality, transparency, and accountability.

Which factors led to revenue growing in H1 2026?

Our first-half performance reflects the successful execution of the strategic transformation we have undertaken over the past several years. Our revenue increased by 68 percent year-on-year, supported by continued operational momentum, disciplined project execution, stronger development activity and ongoing improvements across the business.

A key contributor to this performance was the continued strength of our subsidiaries, which delivered solid operational results and reinforced our diversified business model. Their strong performance, combined with our core real estate activities, played an important role in driving revenue growth and enhancing overall business resilience.

At the same time, our focus on operational efficiency and cost discipline helped us translate this revenue growth into stronger profitability, with gross profit increasing by 41 percent.

More importantly, these results demonstrate that we have successfully transitioned from financial restructuring to sustainable growth, supported by a stronger balance sheet, enhanced earnings visibility and a robust development pipeline.

What is your outlook on the Dubai property market, particularly the residential segment?

We remain highly positive about the outlook for Dubai’s residential real estate market. The market continues to be supported by strong macroeconomic fundamentals, population growth, sustained international investment and rising demand from end-users, all of which are contributing to a healthier and more balanced market.

While geopolitical developments may influence short-term sentiment, Dubai has consistently demonstrated exceptional resilience under the UAE’s wise leadership, supported by a transparent regulatory environment, sustained economic stability and strong global investor confidence. In many cases, periods of regional uncertainty have further reinforced Dubai’s position as a preferred destination for long-term investment.

For us, these market fundamentals provide a strong platform for continued growth. With approximately AED 4 billion ($1.1 billion) of projects under development, AED 3.87 billion ($1.05 billion) in future development revenue yet to be recognised through 2028, and one of the strongest liquidity positions in our recent history, we have clear visibility over future earnings and the ability to continue growing our portfolio while delivering long‑term value for our shareholders.

(Reporting by SA Kader; Editing by Anoop Menon)
